steps.body: To compare any two two-digit numbers: check the tens. If they differ, more tens wins. If they're equal, more ones wins. That one rule handles every pair.
Watch a bigger ten beat bigger ones.

widget.prompt: The marker starts at 48. Drag it to 52.

commonPlacements.feedback: 50 begins the next ten, but 52 has two ones too. Keep moving right.
That copied the 8 ones from 48. The target is 52: 5 tens and 2 ones.

widget.successFeedback: 52 sits to the right of 48. The extra ten matters more than 48's extra ones.
widget.lowFeedback: The marker is below 52. Move right.
widget.highFeedback: The marker is above 52. Move left.

predict.prompt: 52 has fewer ones than 48, but one more ten. Where will 52 sit?
predict.reveal: The marker moves right to 52. Five tens beat four tens before the ones are compared.

widget.ltFeedback: The 8 ones look big, but tens come first: 5 tens > 4 tens, so 52 > 48.
widget.eqFeedback: Different tens (5 vs 4), so 52 > 48, not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 52 > 48.

steps.body: Watch out: a bigger ones digit doesn't win if the tens are smaller. 39 vs 41: 9 ones looks big, but 3 tens is less than 4 tens, so 39 < 41.

widget.gtFeedback: The 9 ones look big, but tens come first: 3 tens < 4 tens, so 39 < 41.
widget.eqFeedback: Different tens (3 vs 4), so 39 < 41, not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 3 tens is less than 4 tens, so 39 < 41, even though 9 > 1 in the ones.

steps.body: Equal numbers have the same tens and ones. Otherwise, the first place that differs decides it — always starting from the tens.

widget.gtFeedback: 70 isn't greater than 70 — same 7 tens and same 0 ones, so they're equal.
widget.ltFeedback: 70 isn't less than 70 — same 7 tens and same 0 ones, so they're equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — same tens and same ones, so 70 = 70.

steps.body: One rule compares any two-digit numbers: tens first, then ones.
takeaways: Same tens and ones? The numbers are equal.
steps.teaser: you've finished Tens & Ones — bundling, expanded form, adding tens, and comparing.

concept.body: Compare any two-digit numbers with one rule: check the tens first — more tens wins; if the tens tie, more ones wins; if both match, they're equal. 52 vs 48: 5 tens > 4 tens, so 52 > 48.

explanationVariants: 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 52 > 48.
Tens first: 52 has more tens than 48.
